clue.text: Is unable to get a girl into bed!

indicators.note: getting one thing into another places it inside, so the girl's name goes within the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A frustrated suitor complains that he never manages to take a girl to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the cheeky surface; 'Is unable' is the definition, not part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannot is the plain negative form of can, meaning lacking the ability to do something.

clue.text: Film head office put in a container

indicators.note: putting something in a box places it inside, so this letter goes within the box word

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard container

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of office is kept

parts.note: the first letter of office

explanation.surface: A film company's head office is housed in a shipping container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head office' reads as a company's headquarters, but 'head' only picks the opening letter of 'office'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is an animated film, such as a Disney short.

clue.text: Famous, but having no time to meet journalist

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A celebrity too busy to give an interview to a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or celebrated, as in a noted author.

clue.text: Material for musical instrument and street guide turned up

parts.note: an organ is a keyboard instrument

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so the guide's letters run backwards

parts.note: the A-Z is a British street atlas of a city

explanation.surface: Someone shops for fabric to make a cover for an organ and a road atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is the standard British street map book, especially of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, sheer fabric made of silk or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Sixty seconds on motorway in an Australian pick-up

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1
taken as written
a ute (utility vehicle) is the Australian name for a pick-up truck

explanation.surface: Someone spends a brief spell on the motorway riding in an Australian truck.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the British road-numbering prefix for motorways.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is the unit of time made up of exactly sixty seconds on any clock.

clue.text: Native using pub scoffed

parts.note: an inn is a pub
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A local who ate greedily at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Native and innate both describe qualities someone is born with rather than acquired.

clue.text: Girl beaten but not ashamed

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
to be bashed is to be beaten

explanation.surface: A girl loses a contest but holds her head high.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabashed means without embarrassment, entirely unembarrassed by something.

clue.text: Came out in front of entrance and mingled

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of entrance
things mingled together have merged

explanation.surface: Guests stepped out by the entrance and chatted with the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, as from a doorway or hiding place.

clue.text: Decline to discourage one with a speech

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
I is the Roman numeral one
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to put a speaker off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb, refuse, but is a noun meaning worsening.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterioration is a gradual worsening in condition or quality.

clue.text: Court order author Elizabeth to leave

indicators.note: the queen's initials are told to go away, so they are removed from the writer word

parts.note: an author is a writer
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A court orders a writer called Elizabeth to quit the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: WRITER loses ER to leave WRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written command issued by a court ordering someone to act or refrain.

clue.text: Raw egg, as ordered, and plums

parts.note: raw in the sense of inexperienced is green

indicators.note: letters that are ordered are put into a new sequence, so these are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A breakfast order: a raw egg, done as requested, along with some plums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raw egg' reads as a unit, but 'Raw' stands alone as a synonym and only 'egg, as' is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Greengages are a variety of small sweet green dessert plum.

clue.text: Where a pupil takes on a college fellow

parts.note: L is a learner, as on learner-driver plates
taken as written
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Someone asks in which place a student goes on to become a college fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'Where', answered by a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a place, the British capital city, which answers the question word asking for a location.

clue.text: Using badly set compass, gets cut off

indicators.note: something done badly comes out jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
compass in the sense of scope or extent is range

explanation.surface: A hiker relying on a wrongly set compass ends up stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' looks like the navigation tool but means extent or range.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate or separate someone, leaving them isolated from family or friends.

clue.text: Note I'm acting strangely, which is puzzling

indicators.note: acting strangely means behaving out of the usual order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is a musical note
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone observes their own odd behaviour and finds it baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like 'observe' but is the musical note E, joined to the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic describes something mysterious and hard to interpret, like a riddle.

clue.text: Doctor ruins game making bloomers

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or alter it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic wrecks a match by committing silly blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like mistakes or knickers, but means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraniums are popular flowering plants, things that bloom, so playfully bloomers.

clue.text: Dropped in to wish Edwina well

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding, completing the picture of a get-well visit

explanation.surface: A friend drops by to give Edwina their good wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: wiSH EDwina holds the answer across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to let it fall or cast it off, as a tree drops leaves.

clue.text: Conservatives are causing trouble

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political complaint that the Tories are making a nuisance of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Care in the sense of worry or anxiety is a burden that troubles the mind.

clue.text: Oriental church in a different see

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: a different version is changed from the original, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Eastern church that belongs to another bishop's diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese, which fits the church picture but is just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese, from China, is an example of something Oriental, from the East.

clue.text: Officer on two-masted vessel I read about

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship

indicators.note: about suggests moving round, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor recounts reading about an officer serving aboard a two-masted ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army rank, commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Beginning of a good book

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an origin or coming into being
second meaning: the opening book of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.walkthrough: The Good Book is the Bible, and its first book tells of creation, so the word means both an origin and that book.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means origin or creation, and is also the name of the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: Once named becomes agitated

parts.note: ex means former, once
to cite someone is to name them

explanation.surface: Someone gets flustered after being mentioned by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited means stirred up or worked up emotionally, roused and restless.

clue.text: Office machine company needing support

parts.note: Co. abbreviates company
a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A firm's photocopier is in need of maintenance backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier, or photocopier, is a standard piece of office equipment for duplicating documents.

clue.text: Shows you the way to endorse an appointment

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the third person; the answer is the bare verb or the noun

parts.note: to endorse a document is to sign it
an appointment to a job is a post

explanation.surface: Advice on how to approve someone's appointment to a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is a roadside marker that points travellers in the right direction.

clue.text: Warning if reversing 100mph on a slippery surface

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the speed word is read from end to start

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred miles per hour
ice makes a slippery surface

explanation.surface: A road-safety caution about doing a hundred in reverse on an icy road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing the ton' is British slang for driving at 100mph.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice is a formal announcement or advance warning, as in giving notice.

clue.text: Number inside both reels

indicators.note: inside says the letters lie within the following words, spanning their join

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A film buff notes a figure appears on each of two reels.
explanation.walkthrough: boTH REEls hides the answer across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a cardinal number, the integer after two.

clue.text: Description of certain plants, for example, illuminated externally

indicators.note: something lying externally is on the outside, so the bright word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: illuminated means lit up, luminous
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A botanical label noting that some plants glow when lit up.
explanation.walkthrough: LU(EG)MINOUS: the abbreviation sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Leguminous describes plants of the pea and bean family, which bear pods.

clue.text: Consider tear needs repairing

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken and must be put back together differently

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a rip in a garment ought to be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to regard or judge it in a certain way, as in rating someone highly.

clue.text: Make certain nurse turns key

indicators.note: turns suggests twisting into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A careful nurse turns the key to check that a door is locked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is the musical key E, not a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to guarantee or secure that something happens.

clue.text: Very big nurse is after the port!

parts.note: OS is outsize, the clothing-size label
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A sailor's joke that a huge nurse wants nothing but a bottle of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is the Belgian ferry port.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a harbour town on the Belgian coast with ferry links to Britain.
